name: a-fog-swallowed-park
prompt: A tall portrait illustration made with a steel dip pen and diluted grey ink brushed wet onto brittle, tea-yellowed newsprint, so the paper's own grain and foxing show through the washes. We look down from a little above at a small public garden in 1919, early morning, swallowed by a dense, low, motionless fog. Visibility ends a few strides from the bench: iron railings and the trunks of plane trees are inked crisply at the front, then go faint, then become only pale smudges, then nothing, as if the wash has eaten them. One cast-iron park bench sits dead centre, the only thing drawn with full, hard, black line. On its left end sits a fat rich man in a long dark overcoat and a tall silk top hat, a heavy black mass laid down in dense crosshatching, a shade too large for the bench, which sags under him; the upper part of his hat bleeds softly upward into the grey fog with no edge. His face is half shadow, small pale eyes, a thin satisfied smile, and he lifts one fat gloved hand lazily from the wrist in a bored, dismissive brush-off. At the far right end, small and drawn in thin, broken, faltering line, a young soldier in a worn army greatcoat with one trouser leg pinned up and a wooden crutch beside him, his outline thinning into the mist as if he is already being erased. Flat, sourceless, shadowless dawn light; palette of ink black, three greys of wash and the yellow of old paper, nothing else. Wide empty fog fills the top third of the frame. No lettering, captions, signatures or text anywhere in the picture. Thanks.

name: a-gaslamp-silent-film-still
prompt: One surviving frame of a lost 1919 horror reel, upright portrait framing. Night in a public garden, everything gone except a cast-iron bench and a single gas lantern hanging on a bracket straight above it, so its flame pours down like a spotlight from the ceiling of the dark. On the bench, directly under that flame, a bloated plutocrat in a stovepipe silk hat, black frock coat strained over his belly, a gold fob chain catching one spark. The overhead glare drops the hat brim's shadow across his eyes, leaving two bottomless black pits where they should be, while below them a powdered, chalk-pale face holds a courteous little smile that glows almost white; his lip rouge prints as ink, as red always did on that blue-only stock. Wearily, a gloved hand dangles and flaps once at the man beside him: a hollow-cheeked infantryman home from the front, army greatcoat too big, one leg ending at the knee with the trouser folded and pinned, a plain wooden crutch laid across his lap. The veteran sits past the edge of the lamplight and dissolves into the night, only his fingers on the crutch and the line of one cheekbone faintly showing. Static camera at seated eye level, square-on, a medium shot of the pair placed in the lower half of the frame, the upper third an unbroken black void above the lantern kept clear for a caption. The emulsion of a hand-cranked early nitrate print: blown-out whites slamming into pure black with almost nothing in between, coarse clotted grain, hairline scratches running top to bottom, flecks of dust, edges going soft, a round iris mask darkening all four corners. Monochrome, photochemical, no smooth digital finish, no lettering anywhere. Thanks.

name: a-his-shadow-arrives-first
prompt: A two-colour reduction linocut, rust-orange laid down first and heavy black printed over it from the same recut block, pressed onto coarse cream paper, the two inks sitting slightly out of register. There is no soft shading anywhere: every mark is a hacked, splintered gouge, raw and angry, as though carved in a hurry. We lie at gravel level on a park path in 1919, right beside the scuffed rubber foot of a wooden crutch looming huge and close in the lower left corner, and the whole view is tipped several degrees so the path climbs steeply away from us. High up and far off sits a park bench, drawn tiny and needle-sharp: a corpulent plutocrat wearing a towering stovepipe hat and a buttoned morning coat, flicking his fingers outward in a lazy brush-off, and beside him a gaunt veteran with a cropped head and a frayed khaki tunic, one leg ending at the knee, the empty trouser folded and pinned. Behind them a swollen dusk sun hangs low on the horizon, a burning orange disc with chiselled rays. From it the plutocrat's shadow spills down the path toward us, grotesquely oversized and stretched, the hat drawn out into a black chimney and the belly into a heaving blot, rearing over the seated veteran and running all the way down the gravel until it touches the crutch beside us. The veteran's shadow is only a frail cracked splinter. Leafless trees bend inward from both sides like bars. Above the bench, a wide strip of raw streaked orange sky stays completely empty. No writing, lettering, numbers or signs anywhere. Thanks.

name: b-blurred-behind-the-nurse
prompt: Vertical night photo, lens wide open so only the closest subject holds focus. Close to camera, crisp down to the drizzle beads on her eyelashes, an exhausted nurse in wrinkled scrubs slouches against the armrest of a public bench, eyes shut, head lolling sideways, staff badge on a lanyard tangled around her collar, a paper face mask dangling from an ear, palms upturned and slack on her thighs. The bench is cast iron and timber slats, its green coat blistered and scabbed off in flakes over brown rust, puddles sitting in the gaps. Seated further down that very bench, a little behind her and smeared by the shallow focus into soft blobs, waits an enormous figure: dark bulky coat, a tall stovepipe hat, a pale round face with a broad white grin, and a raised palm flicking toward her in a dismissive wave. Out of focus he is mostly a heavy black silhouette; you have to squint to be sure he is real, and he seems to lean slightly closer than anyone should. One sodium-vapour streetlamp behind them drowns everything in flat amber monochrome, so colours die and skin turns waxy; its glow swells into a hazy halo in the fine mist, and beyond its reach the park sinks into murky darkness. The top third is empty black wet sky dissolving into haze. Palette of amber, rust brown and inky black, a hint of cold teal left in her scrubs; visible grain, bloom around the lamp, no text, signage or writing. Thanks.

name: b-crosshatched-grin-closeup
prompt: Vertical black-ink drawing on off-white paper, a single face pressed so close to the viewer that it overflows every border: a plump, well-fed gentleman, ears and temples cropped away, nothing at all behind him but his own skin. Across the top edge lies the stiff brim of a tall silk hat, sealing him in like a coffin lid. His brow and both eye sockets are dug out with layer upon layer of short broken hatching strokes, each patch running a new direction, stacked until they read as near-solid black pits; lower down, across his cheeks, nose and heavy jowls, the strokes thin out into dense pinprick stipple, like pores under a magnifier. From the darkness of the left socket one eye stares out, rendered with fanatical precision, wet lid rims, single lashes, a hard white highlight on the cornea, and curled small inside that wet shine is his reflection of a lone exhausted nurse in rumpled scrubs sitting hunched on a slatted park bench, the only other living soul shown. His smile is courteous and much too broad, stretching nearly ear to ear, lips pulled thin over a tidy row of tiny matching teeth, cheeks puffed into hatched folds. Nib lines scratchy, occasionally splitting, the pressure relentless and obsessive. The drawing ends abruptly beneath his doubled chin and starched wing collar, leaving a wide strip of untouched paper along the bottom. Dead-centre, eye-level framing, claustrophobically near, shadowless even light where all darkness comes from the pen. Pure line and dot, no grey washes, no colour, no lettering. Thanks.

name: b-low-poly-short-draw-distance
prompt: Still grabbed from a 1998 home-console horror game running at 320 by 240 pixels, a little before dawn: one public bench on a cracked tarmac path, watched by a camera fixed high up on a lamp post and pitched sharply downward, the angle of a cheap surveillance feed nobody checks. Everything is built from few polygons, with blunt angular limbs and corners that do not quite meet; tiny low-resolution textures are stretched across them and bend in the wrong directions, so the slats, the litter bin and the strip of grass look smeared and rippled; every shade is broken into a coarse checkerboard dither and every outline steps like a staircase. Two or three metres past the bench a dense grey-green haze stops the world dead, flat and featureless, filling the upper portion of the picture as blank space. On the left end of the bench a worn-out nurse in faded blue scrubs slumps forward with her elbows on her knees, lit by a single cold cone of light, her body as blocky and blurred as the bin beside her, her face only a few muddy pixels. On the right end, impossibly, sits an obese gentleman wearing a tall black silk hat and a heavy frock coat, rendered with photographic sharpness as though he belongs to a different, far more expensive machine: crisp wool weave, pin-sharp watch chain, damp pink skin, heavy chins, a thin patient smile, pale wet eyes lifted straight to the lens. His fingers rise lazily toward her, palm out, brushing her away. The sharpness is what makes him monstrous. Colours of mould, wet cement and old pond water, the nurse's light a dim fluorescent white. No words, numbers, logos, health bars or on-screen interface. Thanks.

name: c-black-painting-on-plaster
prompt: Portrait-format oil painting done directly on a damp, ancient plaster wall: the surface is crazed with fine cracks, blistered and flaking, chalky bare ground breaking through the pigment in pale islands. Jammed against the right edge, a vast pot-bellied plutocrat squats forward on the last few slats of a park bench, swollen so large his shoulders seem to press out through the wall toward us. He wears a battered stovepipe hat and a long dark tailcoat swallowed by shadow; his doughy face is mud and ash, the eyes sunk into dark hollows with one wet point of light each, and a wide crooked grin of yellowed teeth splits it ear to ear. One heavy gloved hand floats up near his jaw, limp at the wrist, flicking a lazy, bored brush-off at nobody. Paint is slapped on fast with a broad brush and a palette knife, dragged, scraped back, left to drip down his coat. The single clean white in the whole picture is his starched shirt bib, glowing under the chins. Leftward the bench gives out after two slats and sinks into soot; everything else is an immense brushy darkness of umber and lamp-black, faint grey ghosts where earlier figures were painted out and lost, as if he alone outlived whatever else was on this wall. The top half is nearly empty smoky gloom, calm enough for a caption. Seen square-on and close, at standing height, as if in a dim room before the wall; a weak raking light from one side picks out the ridges of paint. Colours restricted to yellow ochre, raw umber, ash grey and black, plus that one white. No text, no lettering, no signature. Thanks.

name: c-the-only-still-thing
prompt: Tall antique silver-gelatin photograph printed from a cracked glass plate, shot by a big wooden view camera locked off at seated eye height, square-on to a cast-iron park bench with wooden slats that sits across the bottom half of the frame, deep focus from front to back. One man occupies the middle of the bench, perfectly frontal, full figure from hat to boots: enormously fat, wealthy, in a tall gleaming stovepipe hat, a frock coat straining over a waistcoat, a gold watch chain looped across his belly, gloved hands, polished spats. His right hand is raised beside his shoulder, palm out, mid-dismissal. He alone is razor sharp, every stitch and whisker crisp, with a wide, calm, unmoving smile and pale eyes that hold the lens without blinking. The plate was left open on a bright overcast day for so long that everyone who came and went has dissolved into translucent drifts of grey: ranks of marching soldiers, a man on a crutch, nurses in scrubs, shoppers, a pram, whirling leaves, layer upon layer of half-erased bodies streaming past and even sitting beside him, faint as fog on a window, none casting a shadow. Only the fat man casts one, a solid black blot under the seat. Tonal range runs from soot black to cold paper white with no colour. The plate itself is decaying: a bluish metallic silvering creeping in from the borders, thin scratches, dust specks, one corner broken off to clear glass, a spidery crack across a lower edge. The top third is an almost blank, blown-out pale sky with a couple of bare twig tips, kept clear. Unsettling through stillness, never gore. No writing, signage or letters. Thanks.

name: c-rust-dust-wasteland
prompt: Portrait-format oil painting in a meticulous, technically exact dystopian surrealist manner: a vast, deep view looking down from high and far away over the remains of a public park, now a desert of drifted rust-coloured powder under a dull brown noon. Bent iron fencing curls over like dead fern fronds and sinks into the dunes; a lone stripped tree, charred and forked, claws at the haze; a fallen cast-iron lamp standard has turned to grey cinder along half its length and is crumbling where it lies. Everything far off melts into airborne grit, layered in fading veils of atmospheric perspective. The sun is a pale bruise behind the murk and the light is flat, heavy and shadowless. Colour is strictly limited to four neighbouring earth tones, yellow ochre, burnt sienna, raw umber and iron-oxide red, with a crusted, granular paint surface and dirty, unevenly overlapping hatch marks that read as grime built up over years. Precisely in the middle of the canvas, very small, sits an unbroken wooden park bench, and on it a stout, heavy-jowled gentleman wearing a tall silk stovepipe hat, an immaculate frock coat, a clean white collar and pale kid gloves, his skin rosy and smooth, untouched by the dust, the single bright, cool note in the entire painting. Knees crossed, he flicks the fingers of his right hand outward in a bored brush-off towards the vacant seat and the dead land, wearing a thin, contented smile, though there is not a living soul for miles to receive it. Overhead, the choking dun haze rolls on unbroken and featureless across a wide band of the picture, a blank stretch of murky air kept bare so words can be laid over it afterwards. The image holds no lettering, words, signs or numerals of any kind. Thanks.
